exposure: Newborns were divided into two subgroups: those with birth weights of 4000 to 4500 grams and those with birth weights above 4500 grams.
newborns with birth weight above 4500 grams
cohort: Patients monitored at the service who had newborns with birth weight equal than or greater than 4000 grams in the period from January 2014 to December 2019.
finding: Birth weight above 4000 grams had a statistically significant impact on the occurrence of neonatal complications, such as hypoglycemia, respiratory distress and 5th minute APGAR less than 7, especially if birth weight was above 4500 grams.
mod_finding: The most common mode of delivery for macrosomic newborns was cesarean section (65%).
